item.title: Bastidas Soccer Academy Training Camp — Wed Jul 29, 9:00 AM — Manheim Central Middle School
item.description:

All boys and girls from any school or district, entering grades 3-8, are invited to attend this premier camp to kick off the fall season. Registration is $200 per player (or $190 each for a sibling group) and will include:
Camp T-shirt USSF Licensed Coaches (including “A” License coach Trajano Bastidas) and USYS ODP Coaches Camp features– league play, king of the hill, soccer dance, small sided games, stations Main focuses– first touch, passing, receiving, finishing, having fun!
Players should arrive at least 10 minutes early each day with proper attire, sneakers, cleats, shin guards, plenty of water, and a snack for the mid-point break. Questions? item.title: Scootin’ for Scoops with Strasburg Scooter Tours — Thu Jul 30 — Strasburg Scooter Tours
item.description:
Enjoy a 5-star Lancaster County ice cream tour experience with Strasburg Scooter Tours. You’ll see rolling farmlands, pass by horse and buggies, and enjoy some of the best Ice Cream in Lancaster County! It’s a stark contrast to the usual fast-paced and congested areas of larger cities. For those craving something different or one of the best romantic date night ideas, join us! We designed this tour to be an experience you can share with someone. We’ll only use Scoot Coupes, so single riders will have to look for someone to bring on the tour. It will be well worth it as you can expect exceptional views. Bond throughout the experience alongside our expert guide and relish some tasty ice cream* as we Ride around the rolling farmland surrounding the Village of Intercourse and Bird-in-Hand, PA. >> Check Out Our Ice Cream Tour in Strasburg, PA Itinerary Some of our past tours have included:

item.title: Thursday Evening Special 26R (A+) (22-24mph) — Thu Jul 30, 6:00 PM
item.description:
Lancaster Bicycle Club (LBC) Meetup 25-ish mile flat *rolling* route. The route is the same each week.
For the experienced group rider in good physical condition and capable of maintaining a steady pace. Few stops if any. Riders unable to maintain classified pace may be dropped. If unsure if this ride is for you, it is recommended you try the "A" ride option first, which leaves from the same location a few minutes later.
Cue sheet and GPX files: [https://ridewithgps.com/routes/42866619](https://ridewithgps.com/routes/42866619)
\*occasionally, additional miles are added mid-loop. Please note the start location is NOT Landis Valley Museum.
Show & Go (please bring a cue if you are not familiar with the route). No Leader (means that this ride will not be cancelled due to weather).
Helmets are mandatory; No ear buds or audible music playing devices. Please bring water, and a basic repair kit (spare tube, tire levers, pump/CO2 inflator).

item.title: Bridges & Brunch with Strasburg Scooter Tours — Fri Jul 31 — Strasburg Scooter Tours
item.description:
Experience a relaxing morning ride through the back roads of Amish Country in Lancaster County, PA. Along the way to a 19th century covered bridge, enjoy the scenery of rolling hills, breathtaking views, and our Amish neighbors going about their daily routines. Itinerary Duration: 1.5-2 hours Some of our past tours have included:
A guided tour of one of Lancaster County’s most beautiful covered bridges An opportunity for a close up of daily life in Amish Country $10 dining voucher to one of two of Strasburg’s favorites brunch spots, Casey Jones’ Restaurant and Speckled Hen*
And each trip is unique, so you never know what we might have in store for you! *Unfortunately, we regret to inform you that some of the food offerings on the tour may not be considered ‘Kosher.’ We apologize for any inconvenience.
Source: Discover Lancaster

item.title: Lancaster Breakfast and History Walking Tour — Fri Jul 31, 9:00 AM — Unique Lancaster
item.description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally!
Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century.
Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI.
But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region.

item.title: Carlisle’s Monday Game Night — Mon Aug 10, 4:30 PM
item.description:
Central PA Game Club Carlisle’s Monday Game Night. Most attendees are playing modern designer games like Ticket to Ride, Catan, Carcassonne, Wingspan, etc. Guests are always welcome to bring classic games (Scrabble, Backgammon, playing cards).
* All ages are welcome.

* Learn a game, bring a game, teach a game.

* Feel free to bring your own!

* You do not need to show up exactly at the start time. Feel free to drop in at any time.

item.title: Being One Online Spiritual Support Group — Mon Aug 17, 7:00 PM
item.description:
Being One Center in Lancaster County Life can be frustrating and distressing! Sometimes we just feel overwhelmed, insecure, or lost!
The good news is, you're not alone!
We warmly invite you to check-in and connect with community in our Online Spiritual Support Group. In each meeting, we will discuss our current stressors and see how we can positively cope using our spiritual tools to overcome these challenges.
Together we can help each other grow and expand our consciousness for these high vibrational times.
Donations Greatly Appreciated!
This Event is lovingly hosted By Anna Bojczuk. Anna is a Registered nurse with over 40 years of experience as well as a gifted Energy worker. Anna is also long-time volunteer and inspiration in the Being One Center Community.
Donations to the Being One Center are greatly appreciated (https://www.paypal.com/donate?token=AzIxMnj72R-pxLPP0cGQILM7OPiZs5zbsOdxGA7LFH60Wkr_0YcLATVAkIHYVjrFl4PP36X2GkDEJbaM)

item.title: Screening of The Golem: How He Came Into the World (1920 Silent Film) — Thu Oct 15, 6:00 PM — Lititz
item.description:

Yiddish Book CenterThe Golem: How He Came into the World (Der Golem, wie er in die Welt kam, 1920) is a German silent horror film directed by Paul Wegener (with Carl Boese) and co-written by Henrik Galeen, based on Gustav Meyrink’s 1915 novel. It is considered a leading example of early German Expressionism and is notable for being the only surviving film in a trilogy of golem-themed works by Wegener.The movie runs 1 hour and 15 minutes. Popcorn and soda will be served.
